# ADR-0053: Pin server processes to NUMA nodes declared on the machine binding

> **Status:** accepted | **Date:** 2026-10-01

**References:** [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md), [RFC-0003](../rfc/RFC-0003.md)

## Context

On shared multi-socket hosts, managed serving measurements vary with load that other sessions place on the CPUs and memory the server happens to use. A downstream operator found engine-level A/B comparisons reliable only after binding the server to the NUMA node that hosts its GPUs. InferLab launches every server process itself and offered no way to apply such a binding. Which node is appropriate, and whether binding helps at all, is a fact about one machine and how it is shared, like its device and port pools; it is not portable server intent.

## Decision

A machine binding MAY declare `numa_nodes`, a nonempty list of distinct NUMA node indices on that machine. Every server process InferLab launches on the binding, engine ranks and InferLab-owned frontends alike, runs bound to those nodes for both CPU placement and memory allocation. A host process runs under `numactl --cpunodebind=<nodes> --membind=<nodes>` prefixed to its resolved command; a containerized process receives the container runtime cpuset for the nodes' CPUs and memory nodes, with the CPU lists read from the launch machine during resolution, dry-run included. A host launch requires numactl on its launch machine, and every declared node must exist there and have CPUs; any such failure, or a probe that does not report every declared node, stops resolution naming the machine. The binding lives in the resolved commands, which dry-run and records already preserve, so it adds no separate record field. Omitting `numa_nodes` keeps today's unbound launch.

## Consequences

Operators on shared hosts can make managed runs as reproducible as their hand-pinned engine runs, and a record shows the binding in the command that ran. Host launches gain a numactl dependency only when a binding asks for pinning. A binding whose devices span NUMA nodes cannot pin per rank; it stays unbound until a workflow needs per-rank derivation. Measurement clients remain unpinned.

## Alternatives Considered

### Declare `numa_nodes` on the machine binding and bind every server process launched on it to those nodes (accepted)

- **Pros:** Matches the operator's own workflow and stays visible in configuration and in the recorded commands, Local machine facts stay in local bindings beside devices and ports
- **Cons:** A placement whose devices span nodes gets one binding for all its processes, so such bindings leave it unset

### Derive each process binding from the NUMA affinity of its assigned GPUs behind an opt-in switch (rejected)

- **Pros:** Covers placements that span nodes, one node per rank
- **Cons:** Adds topology probing and per-rank derivation on every launch machine for a case no workflow has asked for

### Expose a free-form launch wrapper on the machine binding (rejected)

- **Pros:** Could express any launcher prefix
- **Cons:** Cannot bind a containerized process, whose CPUs and memory are set by the container runtime, and turns a typed fact into opaque argv
